name: Chang Chih-ho
bio: Chang Chih-ho (c. AD 750) was a Taoist philosopher who held office under the Emperor Su Tsung. Exiled for some offence, he became a lonely wanderer and called himself the “Old Fisherman of the Mists and Waters.”
The poems here are L. Cranmer-Byng’s version in A Lute of Jade (1909), given with the poet’s name as spelled in those books.

poems.title: A World Apart
poems.author: Chang Chih-ho
poems.text:
The Lady Moon is my lover,
My friends are the oceans four,
The heavens have roofed me over,
And the dawn is my golden door
I would liefer follow the condor
Or the seagull, soaring from ken,
Than bury my godhead yonder
In the dust of the whirl of men.

poems.title: 漁歌子 (Yu ge zi)
poems.author: Chang Chih-ho
poems.text:
西塞山前白鷺飛，桃花流水鱖魚肥。
青篛笠，綠蓑衣，斜風細雨不須歸。
